236			Hidden:                true,
237			DisableFlagParsing:    true,
238			Args:                  MinimumNArgs(1),
239			Short:                 "Request shell completion choices for the specified command-line",
240			Long: fmt.Sprintf("%[2]s is a special command that is used by the shell completion logic\n%[1]s",
241				"to request completion choices for the specified command-line.", ShellCompRequestCmd),
242			Run: func(cmd *Command, args []string) {
243				finalCmd, completions, directive, err := cmd.getCompletions(args)
244				if err != nil {
245					CompErrorln(err.Error())
246					// Keep going for multiple reasons:
247					// 1- There could be some valid completions even though there was an error
248					// 2- Even without completions, we need to print the directive
249				}
250	
251				noDescriptions := cmd.CalledAs() == ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
252				if !noDescriptions {
253					if doDescriptions, err := strconv.ParseBool(getEnvConfig(cmd, configEnvVarSuffixDescriptions)); err == nil {

255					}
256				}
257				noActiveHelp := GetActiveHelpConfig(finalCmd) == activeHelpGlobalDisable
258				out := finalCmd.OutOrStdout()
259				for _, comp := range completions {
260					if noActiveHelp && strings.HasPrefix(comp, activeHelpMarker) {
261						// Remove all activeHelp entries if it's disabled.
262						continue
263					}
264					if noDescriptions {
265						// Remove any description that may be included following a tab character.
266						comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\t", 2)[0]
267					}
268	
269					// Make sure we only write the first line to the output.
270					// This is needed if a description contains a linebreak.
271					// Otherwise the shell scripts will interpret the other lines as new flags
272					// and could therefore provide a wrong completion.
273					comp = strings.SplitN(comp, "\n", 2)[0]
274	
275					// Finally trim the completion.  This is especially important to get rid
276					// of a trailing tab when there are no description following it.
277					// For example, a sub-command without a description should not be completed
278					// with a tab at the end (or else zsh will show a -- following it
279					// although there is no description).
280					comp = strings.TrimSpace(comp)
281	
282					// Print each possible completion to the output for the completion script to consume.
283					fmt.Fprintln(out, comp)
284				}
285	
286				// As the last printout, print the completion directive for the completion script to parse.
287				// The directive integer must be that last character following a single colon (:).
288				// The completion script expects :<directive>
289				fmt.Fprintf(out, ":%d\n", directive)
290	
291				// Print some helpful info to stderr for the user to understand.
292				// Output from stderr must be ignored by the completion script.
293				fmt.Fprintf(finalCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Completion ended with directive: %s\n", directive.string())
294			},

300			// This reduces possible side-effects of creating such a command;

316	func (c *Command) getCompletions(args []string) (*Command, []Completion, ShellCompDirective, error) {
317		// The last argument, which is not completely typed by the user,
318		// should not be part of the list of arguments
319		toComplete := args[len(args)-1]
320		// Copy trimmedArgs to a new slice to avoid mutating the caller's
321		// backing array (which may be os.Args) when later appending "--".
322		trimmedArgs := make([]string, len(args)-1)
323		copy(trimmedArgs, args[:len(args)-1])
324	
325		var finalCmd *Command
326		var finalArgs []string
327		var err error
328		// Find the real command for which completion must be performed
329		// check if we need to traverse here to parse local flags on parent commands
330		if c.Root().TraverseChildren {
331			finalCmd, finalArgs, err = c.Root().Traverse(trimmedArgs)
332		} else {
333			// For Root commands that don't specify any value for their Args fields, when we call
334			// Find(), if those Root commands don't have any sub-commands, they will accept arguments.
335			// However, because we have added the __complete sub-command in the current code path, the
336			// call to Find() -> legacyArgs() will return an error if there are any arguments.
337			// To avoid this, we first remove the __complete command to get back to having no sub-commands.
338			rootCmd := c.Root()
339			if len(rootCmd.Commands()) == 1 {
340				rootCmd.RemoveCommand(c)
341			}
342	
343			finalCmd, finalArgs, err = rootCmd.Find(trimmedArgs)
344		}
345		if err != nil {
346			// Unable to find the real command. E.g., <program> someInvalidCmd <TAB>
347			return c, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveDefault, fmt.Errorf("unable to find a command for arguments: %v", trimmedArgs)
348		}
349		finalCmd.ctx = c.ctx
350	
351		// These flags are normally added when `execute()` is called on `finalCmd`,
352		// however, when doing completion, we don't call `finalCmd.execute()`.
353		// Let's add the --help and --version flag ourselves but only if the finalCmd
354		// has not disabled flag parsing; if flag parsing is disabled, it is up to the
355		// finalCmd itself to handle the completion of *all* flags.
356		if !finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing {
357			finalCmd.InitDefaultHelpFlag()
358			finalCmd.InitDefaultVersionFlag()
359		}
360	
361		// Check if we are doing flag value completion before parsing the flags.
362		// This is important because if we are completing a flag value, we need to also
363		// remove the flag name argument from the list of finalArgs or else the parsing
364		// could fail due to an invalid value (incomplete) for the flag.
365		flag, finalArgs, toComplete, flagErr := checkIfFlagCompletion(finalCmd, finalArgs, toComplete)
366	
367		// Check if interspersed is false or -- was set on a previous arg.
368		// This works by counting the arguments. Normally -- is not counted as arg but
369		// if -- was already set or interspersed is false and there is already one arg then
370		// the extra added -- is counted as arg.
371		flagCompletion := true
372		_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))
373		newArgCount := finalCmd.Flags().NArg()
374	
375		// Parse the flags early so we can check if required flags are set
376		if err = finalCmd.ParseFlags(finalArgs); err != nil {
377			return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveDefault, fmt.Errorf("Error while parsing flags from args %v: %s", finalArgs, err.Error())
378		}
379	
380		realArgCount := finalCmd.Flags().NArg()
381		if newArgCount > realArgCount {
382			// don't do flag completion (see above)
383			flagCompletion = false
384		}
385		// Error while attempting to parse flags
386		if flagErr != nil {
387			// If error type is flagCompError and we don't want flagCompletion we should ignore the error
388			if _, ok := flagErr.(*flagCompError); !ok || flagCompletion {
389				return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveDefault, flagErr
390			}
391		}
392	
393		// Look for the --help or --version flags.  If they are present,
394		// there should be no further completions.
395		if helpOrVersionFlagPresent(finalCmd) {
396			return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp, nil
397		}
398	
399		// We only remove the flags from the arguments if DisableFlagParsing is not set.
400		// This is important for commands which have requested to do their own flag completion.
401		if !finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing {
402			finalArgs = finalCmd.Flags().Args()
403		}
404	
405		if flag != nil && flagCompletion {
406			// Check if we are completing a flag value subject to annotations
407			if validExts, present := flag.Annotations[BashCompFilenameExt]; present {
408				if len(validExts) != 0 {
409					// File completion filtered by extensions
410					return finalCmd, validExts, ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt, nil
411				}
412	
413				// The annotation requests simple file completion.  There is no reason to do
414				// that since it is the default behavior anyway.  Let's ignore this annotation
415				// in case the program also registered a completion function for this flag.
416				// Even though it is a mistake on the program's side, let's be nice when we can.
417			}
418	
419			if subDir, present := flag.Annotations[BashCompSubdirsInDir]; present {
420				if len(subDir) == 1 {
421					// Directory completion from within a directory
422					return finalCmd, subDir, ShellCompDirectiveFilterDirs, nil
423				}
424				// Directory completion
425				return finalCmd, []Completion{}, ShellCompDirectiveFilterDirs, nil
426			}
427		}
428	
429		var completions []Completion
430		var directive ShellCompDirective
431	
432		// Enforce flag groups before doing flag completions
433		finalCmd.enforceFlagGroupsForCompletion()
434	
435		// Note that we want to perform flagname completion even if finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing==true;
436		// doing this allows for completion of persistent flag names even for commands that disable flag parsing.
437		//
438		// When doing completion of a flag name, as soon as an argument starts with
439		// a '-' we know it is a flag.  We cannot use isFlagArg() here as it requires
440		// the flag name to be complete
441		if flag == nil && len(toComplete) > 0 && toComplete[0] == '-' && !strings.Contains(toComplete, "=") && flagCompletion {
442			// First check for required flags
443			completions = completeRequireFlags(finalCmd, toComplete)
444	
445			// If we have not found any required flags, only then can we show regular flags
446			if len(completions) == 0 {
447				doCompleteFlags := func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
448					_, acceptsMultiple := flag.Value.(SliceValue)
449					acceptsMultiple = acceptsMultiple ||
450						strings.Contains(flag.Value.Type(), "Slice") ||
451						strings.Contains(flag.Value.Type(), "Array") ||
452						strings.HasPrefix(flag.Value.Type(), "stringTo")
453	
454					if !flag.Changed || acceptsMultiple {
455						// If the flag is not already present, or if it can be specified multiple times (Array, Slice, or stringTo)
456						// we suggest it as a completion
457						completions = append(completions, getFlagNameCompletions(flag, toComplete)...)
458					}
459				}
460	
461				// We cannot use finalCmd.Flags() because we may not have called ParsedFlags() for commands
462				// that have set DisableFlagParsing; it is ParseFlags() that merges the inherited and
463				// non-inherited flags.
464				finalCmd.InheritedFlags().VisitAll(func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
465					doCompleteFlags(flag)
466				})
467				// Try to complete non-inherited flags even if DisableFlagParsing==true.
468				// This allows programs to tell Cobra about flags for completion even
469				// if the actual parsing of flags is not done by Cobra.
470				// For instance, Helm uses this to provide flag name completion for
471				// some of its plugins.
472				finalCmd.NonInheritedFlags().VisitAll(func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
473					doCompleteFlags(flag)
474				})

477			directive = ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
478			if len(completions) == 1 && strings.HasSuffix(completions[0], "=") {

484			if !finalCmd.DisableFlagParsing {
485				// If DisableFlagParsing==false, we have completed the flags as known by Cobra;
486				// we can return what we found.
487				// If DisableFlagParsing==true, Cobra may not be aware of all flags, so we
488				// let the logic continue to see if ValidArgsFunction needs to be called.
489				return finalCmd, completions, directive, nil
490			}
491		} else {

494			for cmd := finalCmd; cmd != nil; cmd = cmd.parent {

499			}

501			if flag == nil {

503				// If TraverseChildren is true on the root command we don't check for
504				// local flags because we can use a local flag on a parent command

527					}
528				}
529	
530				// Complete required flags even without the '-' prefix

552							}
553						}
554					}

557					// Only one of ValidArgs or ValidArgsFunction can be used for a single command.
558					return finalCmd, completions, directive, nil

561				// Let the logic continue so as to add any ValidArgsFunction completions,
562				// even if we already found sub-commands.
563				// This is for commands that have subcommands but also specify a ValidArgsFunction.
564			}

567		// Find the completion function for the flag or command
568		var completionFn CompletionFunc
569		if flag != nil && flagCompletion {
570			flagCompletionMutex.RLock()
571			completionFn = flagCompletionFunctions[flag]
572			flagCompletionMutex.RUnlock()
573		} else {
574			completionFn = finalCmd.ValidArgsFunction
575		}
576		if completionFn != nil {
577			// Go custom completion defined for this flag or command.
578			// Call the registered completion function to get the completions.
579			var comps []Completion
580			comps, directive = completionFn(finalCmd, finalArgs, toComplete)
581			completions = append(completions, comps...)

605		flagName := "--" + flag.Name

607			// Flag without the =
608			completions = append(completions, CompletionWithDesc(flagName, flag.Usage))
609	
610			// Why suggest both long forms: --flag and --flag= ?
611			// This forces the user to *always* have to type either an = or a space after the flag name.
612			// Let's be nice and avoid making users have to do that.
613			// Since boolean flags and shortname flags don't show the = form, let's go that route and never show it.
614			// The = form will still work, we just won't suggest it.
615			// This also makes the list of suggested flags shorter as we avoid all the = forms.
616			//
617			// if len(flag.NoOptDefVal) == 0 {
618			// 	// Flag requires a value, so it can be suffixed with =
619			// 	flagName += "="
620			// 	completions = append(completions, CompletionWithDesc(flagName, flag.Usage))
621			// }
622		}
623	
624		flagName = "-" + flag.Shorthand
625		if len(flag.Shorthand) > 0 && strings.HasPrefix(flagName, toComplete) {
626			completions = append(completions, CompletionWithDesc(flagName, flag.Usage))

635		doCompleteRequiredFlags := func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
636			if _, present := flag.Annotations[BashCompOneRequiredFlag]; present {

639					completions = append(completions, getFlagNameCompletions(flag, toComplete)...)

657	func checkIfFlagCompletion(finalCmd *Command, args []string, lastArg string) (*pflag.Flag, []string, string, error) {

660			// This is important for commands which have requested to do their own flag completion.
661			return nil, args, lastArg, nil

665		trimmedArgs := args
666		flagWithEqual := false
667		orgLastArg := lastArg
668	
669		// When doing completion of a flag name, as soon as an argument starts with
670		// a '-' we know it is a flag.  We cannot use isFlagArg() here as that function
671		// requires the flag name to be complete
672		if len(lastArg) > 0 && lastArg[0] == '-' {
673			if index := strings.Index(lastArg, "="); index >= 0 {
674				// Flag with an =
675				if strings.HasPrefix(lastArg[:index], "--") {
676					// Flag has full name
677					flagName = lastArg[2:index]
678				} else {
679					// Flag is shorthand
680					// We have to get the last shorthand flag name
681					// e.g. `-asd` => d to provide the correct completion
682					// https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1257
683					flagName = lastArg[index-1 : index]
684				}
685				lastArg = lastArg[index+1:]
686				flagWithEqual = true
687			} else {
688				// Normal flag completion
689				return nil, args, lastArg, nil
690			}
691		}
692	
693		if len(flagName) == 0 {
694			if len(args) > 0 {
695				prevArg := args[len(args)-1]
696				if isFlagArg(prevArg) {
697					// Only consider the case where the flag does not contain an =.
698					// If the flag contains an = it means it has already been fully processed,
699					// so we don't need to deal with it here.
700					if index := strings.Index(prevArg, "="); index < 0 {
701						if strings.HasPrefix(prevArg, "--") {
702							// Flag has full name
703							flagName = prevArg[2:]
704						} else {
705							// Flag is shorthand
706							// We have to get the last shorthand flag name
707							// e.g. `-asd` => d to provide the correct completion
708							// https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1257
709							flagName = prevArg[len(prevArg)-1:]

712						// for an invalid value for that flag

727			return nil, args, orgLastArg, &flagCompError{subCommand: finalCmd.Name(), flagName: flagName}
